A couple of questions:

1. Why is it not mentioning [#118714](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118714)? Did you just happen to stumble upon this issue independently?
2. Why is it based on a weeks old commit? It's including [a fix](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118285) that has already been merged. Did you arrive at this fix independently as well?

Either way, this would be similar to what I proposed [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118714#issuecomment-4274122181) I guess, except it's using a `HashMap` to avoid the looping I talked about vaguely, which is potentially worse, since we're now allocating additional memory (and potentially hitting a page fault) for every reported event, which is a high price to pay for this arguably rare edge-case. It's also (deliberately?) relying on the `HashMap` iteration order being the same as the insertion order, since you could otherwise end up emitting the `AREA_BODY_ADDED` and `AREA_BODY_REMOVED` events out of order, which would be bad.

All of that is of course fixable to some degree, but I'd still rather fix this using the [Jolt body caching](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/compare/master...mihe:godot:jolt/reuse-body-ids) approach talked about in #118714, where we preserve the Jolt body until the next physics step, which would prevent `JoltContactListener3D` from emitting the contact event altogether, saving us from having to accommodate for this case anywhere in the area event pipeline.

(Also, I'm certainly no stranger to AI tooling myself at this point, but since this PR is giving me some mild AI vibes, and your past contributions have involved it to some degree, note that Godot's [contribution guidelines](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/pull_requests/pull_request_guidelines.html#ai-assisted-contributions) require that you disclose what parts you used AI for, if at all.)

Yes, it is based on [#118714](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118714) , I didn't stumble on the issue independently, you can see that based on the name of my branch, but I should've mentioned it in the PR regardless.
As for the fix from the weeks old commit, I have not seen that fix and I should've looked more carefully in the git history.

I have used AI for codebase searching related to Jolt inside of Godot, so I'll add a disclosure related to it. I'll try to do this feature properly based on your suggestions.

> I didn't stumble on the issue independently, you can see that based on the name of my branch

I totally missed that somehow, my bad. But yes, a `Fixes #118714` mention in the PR description helps a lot with connecting it to the relevant issue, and makes it so GitHub automatically closes the issue when the PR is merged.

Engaging in the issue discussion beforehand would probably have been a good idea as well in this case, before putting in potentially redundant work.

I appreciate the effort though.

You're of course welcome to still take your PR to its ideal state if you want, but I'd personally rather see the other approach be merged instead.
